title: After the war: scaling down in the 1950s and 60s
summary: He moved to Forestville in 1944, did few jobs in the 50s and 60s, and did not revive until the 1970s.

story.theme_name: Making a living: hard times, day jobs and scarce work
story.community_name: Day jobs: musicians working outside music

blocks.x: So then what happened. The war is over. The war ends that year.

I was living in Forestville. I bought a house out here, this place, that was 35 years ago? 1944. Well, then things -- there wasn't too much to be done then. I did a few things, what free lanced Himber, Bernie Green and radio and television and then I'm gradually getting out of the picture.
Still we have the 50's and 60's. What were you doing in the 50's and 60's.

I didn't do too much, that I can sometimes think of now. There wasn't much around for me to do. Oh, then there was a time I took a job, an office job for a little by this time over a year. My mind's a blank. I didn't -- I did a little -- I can't think offhand.
What you're saying is that after World War II ended, you really started -- scaling down.
That's right, scaling down. I scaled down after that.
How did you support yourself in the 50's and 60's? Didn't do any freelance writing.
Well, as I said, I did a little, yeah, I did a few things here and there. Not much.
It wasn't until the 70's then when some of these projects were undertaken.
